Lemma
[Distinct ends differ at some compact set]

↗ def:space-of-ends

If $\cE _1\ne \cE _2$ are ends of a topological space $X$, then some compact $K\subset X$ determines different components of $X\setminus K$ for $\cE _1$ and $\cE _2$.
Proof

\sketch

Ends are compatible families in the inverse limit $\varprojlim _K\pi _0(X\setminus K)$; unequal families differ at some coordinate.

□
